steps.body: You now have three tools for three addends: make a ten, use a double, or just add in order. Read the numbers, pick a tool, and say why.
steps.narration: You now have three tools for three addends: make a ten, use a double, or just add in order. Read the numbers, pick a tool, and say why.

widget.prompt: Your chosen pair made 9. Join the last addend, 4.
widget.missFeedback: Start at 9 and count on 4: you land on 13.
widget.successFeedback: Landed on 13 — your grouping reached the same total any other route would.

predict.prompt: A strategy changes HOW you group. What must it never change?
predict.reveal: A grouping strategy is only valid if the total survives it; the route may vary freely.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g1t strategy choice.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for g1t strategy choice must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines g1t strategy choice.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

explanationVariants: Read the addends, then pick a tool.
Every valid tool protects the total.

options.label: Any order — all three are small
options.feedback: Correct — with three small addends no grouping is clearly faster, so any order is fine.

options.label: Only left to right is allowed
options.feedback: Addition permits any grouping; left-to-right is a habit, not a rule.

options.label: Make ten first
options.feedback: These addends are too small to reach ten as a pair, so there is no ten to make.

options.label: Use a double
options.feedback: A double is possible here, but with addends this small, any order is just as fast — no strategy saves real time.

hints: The addends can be grouped in any order.
Grouping changes the work, not the total.

widget.prompt: 2 + 4 + 5 = 11. If you group a different pair first, what is the total?

options.label: 11 — the same total
options.feedback: Correct — regrouping changes the order of the work, never the total, so it stays 11.

options.label: 12 — one more
options.feedback: Regrouping moves no counter into the pile, so the total cannot grow past 11.

options.label: 10 — one less
options.feedback: Regrouping takes no counter out of the pile, so the total cannot fall below 11.

options.label: It depends which pair you group
options.feedback: Every grouping of the same three addends reaches the identical total; only the ease changes.

hints: The addends can be grouped in any order.
Grouping changes the work, not the total.

explanationVariants: The numbers decide which is fastest.

options.label: Double 5 makes 10 first
options.feedback: Correct — a ten-partner pair is the fastest opening because ten-plus-something is easy to name.

options.label: Subtract 2 from 5 first
options.feedback: That works but ignores the ten sitting in plain sight, making the last step harder.

options.label: Make a pair of 5 and 2 only
options.feedback: Counting everything from zero throws away the facts already known.

options.label: Start over by counting from zero
options.feedback: Subtracting removes an amount; this problem joins all three.
